_readme: Source of truth for the Little Kettle Valley residents as Easy NPC 7.11.0 presets.
Do not hand-edit the .npc.snbt files. Edit this file and re-run the generator.

Greeting lines live in `greetings` / `greetings_after`. Element 0 of each pool is the headline line the resident has always had; the rest rotate by world day and player name. The generator writes them to pack/kubejs/server_scripts/valley_greetings.js and the NPC's ON_INTERACTION runs `/valley greet <key> <before|after> @initiator`.

meta.path_warning: VERIFIED FROM THE JAR: de.markusbordihn.easynpc.security.PresetSecurity#isAllowedDataPresetPath accepts a data preset ONLY when its resource path starts with 'easy_npc/preset/' or 'easy_npc/api/preset/' (or, for the easy_npc namespace itself, 'preset/' / 'api/preset/'). A resource location of valley:preset/<name>.npc.snbt is REJECTED with 'Rejected data preset ..., because it is not below the expected ... folder.' The working location is valley:easy_npc/preset/<name>.npc.snbt. The compat copy that used to sit under pack/kubejs/data/valley/preset/ was deleted on 2026-09-02; make_npc_presets.py no longer writes it and pack/index.toml no longer lists it.
meta.access_warning: VERIFIED FROM THE JAR: PresetAccess#isUsableByCommand returns false for access:"INTERNAL". The jar's base humanoid template is INTERNAL, so every valley preset sets access:"PUBLIC" or it cannot be imported by command.
meta.open_book_warning: VERIFIED FROM THE JAR: dev.ftb.mods.ftbquests.command.FTBQuestsCommands registers 'open_book' with an optional quest_object string argument and NO player argument; it opens the book for the command SOURCE player. 'ftbquests open_book @initiator' is therefore a syntax error. The action is written as Cmd:"/ftbquests open_book" with ExecAsUser:1b, which is exactly what pack/config/easy_npc/security.cfg already provisions: executeAsUserCommandAllowList.ALL=ftbquests,trigger,me.
meta.perm_level_note: /info_message expands (ActionUtils.MACRO_INFO_MESSAGE) to /title @initiator title {"text":"...","color":"aqua"}. Vanilla /title needs permission level 2, so the greeting actions carry PermLevel:2. PresetSanitizer clamps PermLevel to min(entry, actor level); a server/console import gets serverTrustedCommandLevel=ADMINS (3), so 2 survives. A survival player importing by hand would have it clamped to 0 and the greeting would silently do nothing -- always run the imports from a function, KubeJS, or an op console.
meta.uuid_note: Each preset carries a deterministic data.UUID (uuid5 of 'valley:npc:<key>'). PresetHandler#importPresetData branches on that UUID: if an entity with it already exists it is updated in place, otherwise it is created. That is what makes 'preset import' idempotent and what makes re-importing a resident safe.

arc_gating.mechanism: SCOREBOARD condition on each ON_INTERACTION greeting action
arc_gating.why: PlayerTagCondition ignores the operation field entirely (it is a plain Set#contains), so a player tag cannot express the 'arc not closed yet' half of the pair. ScoreboardCondition honours ConditionOperationType, so one dummy objective per resident gives both halves.
arc_gating.setup_owner: valley_core.js, on server load, before any resident is imported. If an objective is missing, ScoreboardCondition logs 'Scoreboard objective ... does not exist' and BOTH greeting lines stay hidden -- the NPC would still open the book but say nothing.
arc_gating.close_reward: The arc-closing quest adds a command reward: {"type":"command","command":"/scoreboard players set @p <objective> 1","elevate":true,"silent":true}

meta.tag_note: Tags[] round-trips because importPresetData builds the entity from the whole NBT compound. If a future Easy NPC build drops it, re-tag after import with: /tag @e[type=easy_npc:humanoid,limit=1,sort=nearest] add npc_<key>
meta.skin_note: All skins are SkinData Type:"DEFAULT" with a VariantType from the jar's own enums (HumanoidSkinVariant: ALEX ARI EFE KAI MAKENA NOOR STEVE SUNNY ZURI JAYJASONBO PROFESSOR_01 SECURITY_01 KNIGHT_01 KNIGHT_02; HumanoidSlimSkinVariant: ALEX ARI EFE KAI MAKENA NOOR STEVE SUNNY ZURI KAWORRU). No PLAYER_SKIN, no remote URL: those need a network round trip and security.cfg gates URL_RESOURCE behind CREATIVE_PLAYER.

on_interaction_template._note: Every resident's ON_INTERACTION list is exactly this shape. It is written out per NPC below in "on_interaction" so the generator never has to guess; edit it there, not here.
on_interaction_template.greeting_before_arc: {Type:COMMAND, Cmd:'/info_message <greeting>', ExecAsUser:0b, PermLevel:2, ConditionDataSet:[{Type:SCOREBOARD, Name:<objective>, Operation:LESS_THAN, Value:1}]}
on_interaction_template.greeting_after_arc: {Type:COMMAND, Cmd:'/info_message <greeting_after>', ExecAsUser:0b, PermLevel:2, ConditionDataSet:[{Type:SCOREBOARD, Name:<objective>, Operation:GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS, Value:1}]}
on_interaction_template.open_book: {Type:COMMAND, Cmd:'/ftbquests open_book', ExecAsUser:1b, PermLevel:0}  -- never conditional

npcs.name: Marnie Ashcombe
npcs.register: Warm and presumptive. Talks to you like you already live here. Flour on her sleeves.
npcs.greeting: There you are. Kettle is on and I baked too much bread again.
npcs.greeting_after: Full room tonight. Sit down before I give your chair away.

placements.source: proposed (doc says 'seated positions', gives no coords)
proposed (doc says 'marks outside the Works', gives no coords)

greetings: There you are. Kettle is on and I baked too much bread again.
Sit down. You've got that look people get when they've been carrying something heavy up a hill.
I put a loaf by for you. Don't tell Pip, he counts them.
The Hearth's been lit in this room for thirty years. Some of those years it was the only thing that was.
Eat something. I'm not asking.
greetings_after: Full room tonight. Sit down before I give your chair away.
I called it my inn this morning. Out loud, to Oda. I did not correct myself.
I put a loaf by for you. Same as you put one by for me in February, only mine is better.
The Hearth is lit, the oven is lit and the rooms upstairs are lit. Three fires. I keep counting them.
Eat something. I cooked for fifteen tonight and there is still too much, which is the right amount.

npcs.name: Bram Tolliver
npcs.register: Gruff for about four minutes. Imperative, short, teaches by making you hold things.
npcs.greeting: Do not just stand there. Hold this, and do not let it slip.
npcs.greeting_after: Wheel is turning. Sixty years I waited. Come and look at it.

placements.source: story-final.md 12.5 (the only Act IV position the doc fixes -- he pulls the lever at ~0 ~2 ~0)

greetings: Do not just stand there. Hold this, and do not let it slip.
Mm. You're back. Don't touch the shaft, it's set.
If a thing judders, look at the shaft. It's always the shaft.
My father cut that stock. Label's still on the crate. That's all I'll say about it.
greetings_after: Wheel is turning. Sixty years I waited. Come and look at it.
Sixty-four years and that wheel's turned for two of them. Both since you came.

npcs.name: Oda Vance
npcs.register: Brisk and dry. Ledger under one arm. Transactional affection.

arc.closing_quest: Pay 120 Valley Scrip at Oda's Counter

npcs.greeting: Shelves are thin and my ledger is thinner. What do you need.
npcs.greeting_after: Books balance. Eleven years. Here, take the ledger. I mean it.
greetings: Shelves are thin and my ledger is thinner. What do you need.
Ledger's open. It always is. That's rather the trouble with a ledger.
I've counted the lamps again. I know. You don't have to say it.
Buy something or don't, but stand out of the doorway.
greetings_after: Books balance. Eleven years. Here, take the ledger. I mean it.
Eleven years I kept the book of an empty shop. Now it's the book of a shop.

npcs.name: Nella Brightwater
npcs.register: Flat, short, deadpan. Permanently damp and unbothered by it.

arc.closing_quest: Glaze the Cold Frame and Grow Four Crops Out of Season

npcs.greeting: Lake is in a mood. So am I. Bring a rod anyway.
npcs.greeting_after: Turns out I like growing things. Do not make it strange.

placements.event: First placement (Act II cozy line, Q26 dredging)
placements.source: proposed (the doc introduces her in Act II but fixes no spawn offset)

greetings: Lake is in a mood. So am I. Bring a rod anyway.
Fish aren't biting. Sit down anyway.
Boat's still beached. I know what you're going to say. Don't.
Quiet down here. That's not a complaint.
Good spot's past the reeds. Don't tell everyone.
greetings_after: Turns out I like growing things. Do not make it strange.
Fish aren't biting. Doesn't matter — the tomatoes are.
Boat's mended. Took one afternoon. I had been calling it a week's work since before you came.
Good spot's past the reeds. Tell people. I have decided I don't mind a crowd.

npcs.name: Halden Root
npcs.register: Quiet, slow, ancient-seeming. Answers a question with tea first.
npcs.greeting: Sit a while. Tea first, then whatever it is you came to ask.
npcs.greeting_after: The cellar door is open and I am not carrying it alone now.

placements.event: First placement (Act I cozy line, herbal starts)
placements.source: proposed (hedge garden and still; the doc fixes no offset)
story-final.md 7 (he reads the last page; stand him at the sign, which the finale sets at ~0 ~1 ~-3)

greetings: Sit a while. Tea first, then whatever it is you came to ask.
Kettle's on. Everything else can wait ten minutes; it always could.
The hedge doesn't need me. That's rather why I like it.
Josie planted the first row of that. I only ever kept it trimmed.
Green tea, or the strong one? The strong one is a decision.
greetings_after: The cellar door is open and I am not carrying it alone now.
Kettle's on. The book is open on the table and there are two chairs at it now.
I read her shorthand out loud. Four years I let people think it was the hedge keeping me here.
Josie planted the first row. I have planted the second, which took me rather longer than it should have.
Green tea, or the strong one? Nobody has been ill since November, so have the strong one.

npcs.name: Tobin Gale
npcs.register: Twenty-three, over-caffeinated, unreasonably delighted by rocks. Talks in a rush.
npcs.greeting: You own a pickaxe. Good. Look at this rock. No, really look.
npcs.greeting_after: Bram said good work. Out loud. I have not stopped hearing it.

placements.event: First placement (Act II tech line, the survey)
placements.source: proposed (north-ridge side of the square; the doc fixes no offset)
story-final.md 12.7 ('Tobin already inside, talking'); offset proposed

greetings: You own a pickaxe. Good. Look at this rock. No, really look.
This one has quartz all through it. Nobody in this valley cares about quartz. I care enormously.
I've marked it twice. The second set's in pink. Ignore the pink.
I haven't slept, but that's not new information.
greetings_after: Bram said good work. Out loud. I have not stopped hearing it.
Look at this rock. It is the same rock. I keep it in my pocket now, which Bram says is normal.
The pink marks were right. Nobody has said so out loud, and I am being very calm about it.
Nobody believed me about the seam and now there's a mine, so.
I haven't slept. The rig comes up the road when the road dries, and the road is drying.

npcs.name: Wisp
npcs.role: Ribbit forager, from the reed village downstream
npcs.register: Cheerful, carries too much, sentences come out slightly wrong and it never bothers them.
npcs.greeting: You are come! I bring basket. Eat the purple one first, yes.
npcs.greeting_after: Two villages, one place now. My people sleep warm at the inn.

placements.source: proposed (doc names the destination in 12.7, fixes no offset)

greetings: You are come! I bring basket. Eat the purple one first, yes.
You walk far today? Sit. I keep the good toadstools.
Marsh is quiet, town is loud. Both is good. Different good.
My people ask about you. I say: is the one who came and asked.
I found a red one. I did not eat it. I am learning to not eat first.
greetings_after: Two villages, one place now. My people sleep warm at the inn.
You walk far today? Sit. I keep the good toadstools in the inn now, in a cupboard with a door.
Marsh is quiet, town is loud. I sleep in the loud one now. Is strange. I like.
My people do not ask about you now. They ask you. Is better, I think.
Purple one grows in the warm glass house in winter now. I did not know it could do that.

npcs.name: Pip Ashcombe
npcs.register: Nine. Runs everywhere. Names everything. Says the true thing immediately.
npcs.greeting: The duck is called Biscuit. I decided it in about one second and I am not changing it.
npcs.greeting_after: I have a real job now. The duck supervises. Mostly badly.

placements.source: proposed (the duckling is at the table and is served first)
proposed (he rings the hand bell; the playsound is on @a, so any mark works)
proposed (he rings the bell at the end)

greetings: The duck is called Biscuit. I decided it in about one second and I am not changing it.
The duck went in the water bucket. On purpose, I think. It's fine.
I'm allowed in the mill now if I don't touch anything. I touch nothing.
Aunt Marnie says I ask too many questions. How many is too many?
My satchel has a real buckle. Not a pretend one. A real one.
greetings_after: I have a real job now. The duck supervises. Mostly badly.
Biscuit went in the water trough in front of everybody at supper. She meant to. I saw her decide.
I'm allowed to touch things in the mill now. Bram showed me which ones. I remember all of them.
Aunt Marnie says I still ask too many questions. I asked her how many. She is thinking about it.
I'm the one who rings the bell. Nobody else rings it. That was the deal and everybody heard it.

npcs.name: Reed
npcs.register: Wisp's register, shorter. Cheerful, slightly wrong.
npcs.greeting: Wisp says you are the new one. You are less tall than said.

placements.event: The Harvest Supper (Wisp brings three more Ribbits)

greetings: Wisp says you are the new one. You are less tall than said.
You are taller today. No. Same. I was wrong.
Warm floor here. I sit on it. This is my job now.

npcs.name: Sedge
npcs.greeting: I carry too much. Is fine. Is what I am for, mostly.
greetings: I carry too much. Is fine. Is what I am for, mostly.
I carried the whole house. Wisp says I carried one box. We remember it different.
If it is heavy, I am the one. That is the arrangement.

npcs.name: Mudlark
npcs.greeting: The mud here is good mud. You should be proud of this.
greetings: The mud here is good mud. You should be proud of this.
I brought you mud. Good mud. You do not have to keep it.
The lamps make the puddles orange. I look at them a lot.

npcs.name: Puddle
npcs.greeting: Floor is warm and soup is hot. We stay now, I think. Yes. We stay.

placements.event: The Longest Night (the fourth Ribbit arrives with the reed village)

greetings: Floor is warm and soup is hot. We stay now, I think. Yes. We stay.
Soup again tonight. I checked. I check every night.
We stay. I say it out loud so it stays true.

npcs.name: Tess Weaver
npcs.register: Plain, hopeful, slightly out of breath from the road.
npcs.greeting: Saw your noticeboard from the ridge road. Is there a room?
greetings: Saw your noticeboard from the ridge road. Is there a room?
Room's warm. I keep waking up surprised about it.
I'll pay the week, and then probably the year.

npcs.name: Corin Ashe
npcs.role: Act V arrival, roofer and carpenter
npcs.register: Practical, unbothered, states his trade before his name.
npcs.greeting: I mend roofs. Heard this valley has roofs again. Here I am.
greetings: I mend roofs. Heard this valley has roofs again. Here I am.
Third roof this week. Good roofs. Somebody built them right the first time.
Whoever laid that mill thatch knew what they were doing. Was it you?

npcs.name: Mab Oldfield
npcs.register: Old, level, says the heavy thing without decorating it.
npcs.greeting: I left here in the bad winter. I am not leaving twice.
greetings: I left here in the bad winter. I am not leaving twice.
I know this lane. I know which post leans.
I walked out of here in February eleven years ago. I came back in daylight, which is different.
